The depositions were performed on an Optomec LENS 750 system with a 1000W Nd:YAG laser focused to a 0.5 mm spot size.
The initial feasibility specimen (190-0) had a crack that extended from the top surface to the middle region of the third deposited layer.
EBSD analysis showed the deposit in specimen 190-0 had the same crystallographic orientation as the single-crystal substrate.
X-ray radiography revealed cracks in 6 out of 7 selected specimens prior to sectioning, indicating the cracking occurred during deposition.
Increasing the laser power and/or reducing the deposition velocity did not consistently prevent cracking, and in some cases made the cracking more severe.
Preheating the substrate to 400°C and introducing dwell times between layers also did not reliably prevent cracking.
Deposits on both flat and curved regions of the turbine blade surface exhibited the same crystallographic orientation as the underlying substrate.
The columnar grain growth in the deposits aligned with <100> directions in the substrate and the local thermal gradient direction.
The unreliability of the LENS system was identified as a key challenge in consistently producing crack-free deposits.
